title: Standing firm
hookLine: those who say our Lord is Allah and then stand firm, the angels descend on them: don't fear (41:30)
tomorrow: Signs in the horizons and in themselves

cards: A companion named Sufyan ibn 'Abdullah comes to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ with a request. Tell me something about Islam, he says, that I'll never need to ask anyone else about. One thing, to hold for the rest of my life.
It's a big ask, and the answer, recorded in Sahih Muslim, is just two short sentences. The second one is a single word in Arabic, and it's the word Surah Fussilat puts at the center of today's verse.

teach.b: Here's the answer. Say: I believe in Allah. Then be steadfast.
Qul amantu billah, thumma staqim. Now Fussilat, verse thirty.
Pickthall: "Lo! those who say: Our Lord is Allah, and afterward are upright, the angels descend upon them, saying: Fear not nor grieve, but hear good tidings of the paradise which ye are promised."
The same two steps: say it, then stand firm. The word is istiqamah, from a root meaning to stand up straight, like a pole that doesn't lean.

Back on day four hundred thirty-three, this path heard a report from Ibn 'Abbas that a command to stand firm, in Surah Hud, was harder on the Prophet than any other verse. Fussilat shows what's on the other side of it.
The saying is quick, one sentence. The standing firm takes the rest of your life. Early Muslims explained it in their own ways.
Abu Bakr is reported to have said it means not turning to anything besides Allah. 'Umar is reported to have said: stand straight on what you're commanded, and don't dodge around like a fox.
And the reward is not first a prize, but a presence. The angels descend; commentators say at death, and some add the grave and the day of rising.

teach.h: THE ANGELS: DON'T FEAR, DON'T GRIEVE.
teach.b: Their first words: don't be afraid, and don't grieve. In the verse, that's what follows steadiness: company in hard places, and two burdens lifted, the fear of what's coming and the grief for what's gone.
A hadith in Bukhari adds the practical key: the deeds Allah loves most are the ones done constantly, even if they're small.

how: Muslims often quote the hadith 'say: I believe in Allah, then be steadfast' as a summary of the faith, and value small, regular acts of worship kept up over time.

o: a single moment of great courage in battle
staying silent and perfectly still in prayer
standing firm and upright on the path, over time

s: istiqamah means a single brave act
it means standing upright and staying that way, over time.
the angels' first words in 41:30 are don't fear and don't grieve
then good news of the garden that was promised.
a hadith says Allah loves the most constant deeds, even if small

games.q: you ask the Prophet: tell me one thing about Islam I'll never need to ask anyone else. what does he say?
o: say: I believe in Allah, then be steadfast.
games.why: say: I believe in Allah, then be steadfast. two sentences, the same two steps as 41:30.

practice: Sit up straight, spine upright, like a pole that doesn't lean.
Choose one small practice you already do, or this path itself, small enough that you can't fail, and decide to keep it going this week, even on the days it feels like nothing.
Picture yourself keeping it on your worst day, and if you pray, ask for steadiness.

wordCard.voice: Istiqamah. Standing firm, upright, steadfast: what comes after saying our Lord is Allah, and what the angels meet with don't fear, don't grieve. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: standing firm, uprightness, from the root q-w-m, to stand.

carryVoice: Your line: say it, then stand firm. The angels' first words are don't fear, don't grieve. See you tomorrow.
